QF.id: AIFM AIFs in India and Suitability_1

question.text: The SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012 marked a significant transition in India's private capital industry. As a fund manager launching a new vehicle in 2026, which of the following BEST describes the industry-level transformation that the 2012 Regulations catalysed?

answer.text: A shift from a mutual fund industry to a portfolio management services industry with expanded retail access

The transformation of a predominantly Venture Capital and Private Equity industry into a full-fledged Alternative Investment Fund industry covering hedge funds, real estate, infrastructure and family offices
The migration of all offshore hedge funds to onshore status with SEBI now permitting leveraged retail hedge fund distribution
A regulatory convergence where AIFs, PMS and Mutual Funds were merged under a single licensing regime

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook (pp. 78-80), after the 2012 AIF Regulations the industry evolved from a predominantly venture capital and private equity industry into a full-fledged alternative investment industry, spanning real estate, infrastructure and domestic and foreign hedge funds registered under the AIF Regulations, together with UHNI and family office activity. The Trap: Option A conflates PMS with AIFs and is not the transformation described in pp. 78-80. Option C is inaccurate: offshore hedge funds were not auto-migrated to onshore status by the 2012 Regulations. Option D is fabricated: Mutual Funds, PMS and AIFs continue under separate regulatory frameworks. Note: The source describes a broadening of the registered alternatives universe from a VC/PE-only base to a full-fledged AIF industry including hedge funds, real estate and infrastructure, as set out on pp. 78-80.
